description: Workspace AGENTS.md: 'No `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` in library code — propagate errors with `?`.' The .unwrap()s on Mutex locks (memory.rs:286, 450, 461, 509, 521, 576, 632, 679, 774, 866, 940; lib.rs:196, 205, 213, 222, 233, 242, 257, 294, 306, 384, 431, 456) are arguably the canonical exception (Mutex::lock returns PoisonError only on a prior thread panic-with-guard-held, which the workspace's #[forbid(unsafe_code)] makes a programmer-bug case). But the exception is undocumented at every site. — Idiomatic Rust either (a) attaches a single module-level // SAFETY:-style comment or doc block explaining 'these unwraps signal a programmer bug if they fire, see policy', (b) wraps in a single `fn lock_state(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, ...>` helper that documents the assumption once, or (c) converts to .expect with a stable string the panic message can be grepped for. The current state — bare .unwrap() at every site — is the form a new contributor will copy without thinking about the policy. Engineering impact: low operationally (poisoning is rare), high pedagogically for a 'reference implementation' touchstone.
title: Mutex .unwrap() throughout MemoryBackend and MockBackend without panic-policy comment
